title: Check understanding with a task
statement: Decide whether a learner has understood from what they do on a task, not from their own sense of it, because readers judge their own comprehension poorly.
detail: A reading project's research synthesis quotes the RAND Reading Study Group: most child and adult readers have a poor ability to calibrate the success of their comprehension (App. A, pp. 108-109) (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/reading-science/SYNTHESIS.qmd`). The project's practice criteria schedule review on accuracy and latency, not self-report (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D6-practice-durable-mastery.md`, D6.14).

evidence.quote: "most child and adult readers have a poor ability to calibrate the success of their comprehension"
Students in both AI groups overestimated how much they had learned.
Don't treat students' own reports of learning as a success metric.
A minimum dwell is a software prerequisite, not proof the child understood.

citations.ref: RAND Reading Study Group 2002, Reading for Understanding: Toward an R&D Program in Reading Comprehension (MR-1465)
